title: Lehmer GCD OQ-03-OQ-01: Progress and Correctness of the Lehmer Step
description: Formalizes correctness of the Lehmer/Euclidean GCD step: progress (b + (a mod b) < a + b), GCD invariance (gcd(b, a mod b) = gcd(a,b)), and full algorithm correctness (lehmerGcd = Nat.gcd). 11 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: Lehmer (1938) described an optimization of the Euclidean GCD algorithm for large integers using single-precision arithmetic for multiple steps. The mathematical core is the correctness of each Euclidean step (a,b) → (b, a mod b).
overview.problemStatement: Prove the Lehmer step is correct (GCD-invariant) and makes progress (strictly decreases a+b).
overview.proofStrategy: lehmerStep_gcd_invariant: gcd(b, a mod b) = gcd(a, b) from the Euclidean algorithm property. lehmerGcd_progress: (a mod b) < b ≤ a → (a mod b) + b < a + b. lehmerGcd_correct: by well-founded induction, the iterated steps compute Nat.gcd.
keyInsights: **GCD invariance**: gcd(a,b) = gcd(b, a mod b) is the classical Euclidean algorithm property, here applied to the Lehmer step.
**Progress via modular reduction**: a mod b < b, so b + (a mod b) < a + b when 0 < b ≤ a. This ensures termination.
**Correctness by well-founded induction**: the Lehmer algorithm terminates (decreasing sum) and each step preserves GCD, so the final result equals Nat.gcd.

sections.title: Lehmer Step: GCD Invariance, Progress, Correctness
sections.summary: lehmerStep. lehmerStep_gcd_invariant. lehmerGcd_progress. lehmerGcd_correct: lehmerGcd a b = Nat.gcd a b.
sections.mathContext: $\gcd(b, a \bmod b) = \gcd(a, b)$; $b + (a \bmod b) < a + b$ for $0 < b \leq a$.

conclusion.summary: 11 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. Lehmer step correctness and progress proved.
conclusion.implications: The Lehmer GCD algorithm is fundamental to large-number arithmetic. This formalization verifies the core correctness invariant.
openQuestions: Can the Schönhage-Strassen GCD algorithm be formalized?
Can the asymptotic complexity O((log n)²) be proved?
Can the Lehmer step be used to formalize GCD over Gaussian integers?
